name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,347

clue.text: This news might be disseminated in intervals

indicators.note: news that is disseminated is scattered abroad, so these letters are spread and set down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
read as the plural of new, abbreviated N; plurals of abbreviations double the letter, as pp for pages

explanation.surface: Some piece of news gets spread around at regular intervals, like a bulletin on the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is taken as more than one N (new), just as pp stands for pages, giving two Ns to mix with THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a ninth is the interval spanning nine notes of the scale, so several of them are musical intervals.

clue.text: E.g. like samplers from old female servant say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and take a word that is pronounced the same but spelt differently

blocks.note: a handmaid is an archaic word for a female servant

explanation.surface: Embroidered samplers, the clue suggests, were stitched by a household maid in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: A sampler is a piece of embroidery showing off a range of stitches, traditionally worked by hand by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Samplers are needlework pieces stitched manually rather than by machine, an example of craft goods produced personally.

clue.text: Went on a site about special diamonds

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a location goes around the letter that follows it

blocks.note: a as in 'ten pounds a day', meaning for each
taken as written
S is a standard abbreviation for special
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone talked at length about a location known for unusual gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' here means 'for each', as in 'ten pounds a day', a sense easy to miss in a word that usually gives just A.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to carry on doggedly, so the past tense matches 'went on' in the sense of continued.

clue.text: Clad in iron, a baddie for Tolkien's army

indicators.note: to be clad in something is to be wrapped in it, so the villain sits inside the metal's symbol

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
orcs are the brutish villains of Tolkien's Middle-earth

explanation.surface: An armoured villain is recruited into the legions of The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A force is a body of troops, so an army is one example of a military unit of that kind.

clue.text: Being on board between Dover and Calais, he hops on the box

definitions.text: Being on board between Dover and Calais

blocks.clueFragment: Being on board between Dover and Calais
blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: someone riding a surfboard across the English Channel
second meaning: a television viewer who keeps flicking between stations

explanation.walkthrough: Dover and Calais face each other across the English Channel; 'the box' is British slang for television, and hopping is switching programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surfing the English Channel literally, and an idle viewer constantly switching television stations with the remote.

clue.text: Sailor's lounge on fire

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
to lounge is to idle about

explanation.surface: A seaman's lounging area has caught fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burning fiercely with flames is described with this adjective, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: March most of the way to O2 with no info in a 10 state?

indicators.note: going most of the way means stopping just short, so the final letter of the walking word is dropped
info is slang for information, and having none removes that word's synonym from the end of the element's name

blocks.note: a parade is a formal march
O2 is the molecular formula for oxygen
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Walkers head most of the way to the O2 arena in London without any directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 refers to the answer at 10-down, CONTRADICTORY. PARAD(E) + OXY(GEN): the O2 is also a London concert arena, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradoxy is the condition of being paradoxical, a self-contradicting condition, so it describes a contradictory kind of state.

clue.text: Gwen's John and I go paint regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the following words is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Gwen and John decide to go off and do some painting together.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwen is a Welsh name, so 'Gwen's John' asks for the Welsh form of John; the surface hints at the painters Gwen and Augustus John.
explanation.definitionFit: Ioan is the Welsh equivalent of the name John, so a Welsh speaker like Gwen would use it.

clue.text: A phoenix flies round old boy hating aliens

indicators.note: a creature that flies scatters, so the letters of the mythical bird are rearranged
round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters enclose the former pupil

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A firebird circles an old man who resents foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophobia is fear or dislike of foreigners, and 'aliens' is an older word for people from other countries.

clue.text: With cut in business I'll get caught between two Conservatives in disagreement

indicators.note: a cut shortens something, so the word for business loses its final letter
between places the middle letters inside the two party members either side

blocks.note: surface padding: it tells us both party words are used, one at each end
Con is the abbreviation for a Conservative
trade means commerce or business
I, with 'll joining it to what it will get
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Tory is another name for a Conservative

explanation.surface: A businessman facing cuts complains of being trapped between two Conservative politicians who cannot agree.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Conservatives are CON and TORY, the British party's abbreviation and nickname; TRAD(E), I and C go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements that contradict one another are at odds, so the adjective describes things that are in disagreement.

clue.text: Eccentrically suited with nothing drab

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the letters are arranged in an unconventional order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone dressed oddly yet with nothing colourful at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means dull and boring, and drab has the same sense of being lacking in interest.

clue.text: Record Farewell (a musical work)

blocks.note: film or sound that is recorded is 'in the can', so to can is to record
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye

explanation.surface: A farewell record is released, presented as a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make it look like a note on the record; in fact they hold the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition with choir and soloists, often sacred, so it is a piece of classical music.

clue.text: Elite force capturing marketplace square is too clever by half

indicators.note: the special forces unit captures, holding the trading place inside itself

blocks.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
a mart is a market
S is an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Special forces seize a market square in a raid that proves a bit too clever.
explanation.walkthrough: S(MART)AS, then S for square at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartass is an irritating know-all, someone who is too clever by half, an idiom for showing off one's cleverness.

clue.text: Somehow the River Ebro when crossing the middle is so far

indicators.note: crossing out the middle leaves only the outside letters of the river's name
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put in an order of our choosing

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A journey along Spain's River Ebro has reached the halfway point.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is a formal adverb meaning up to this point, so it matches the phrase 'so far' about progress until now.

clue.text: Condition associated with white noise mostly in mobile Military Intelligence lab

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the sound word loses its last letter
in places the shortened word inside the rearranged letters
mobile means able to move, so the letters of the intelligence unit and laboratory shift about

blocks.note: MI is the abbreviation for Military Intelligence
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: White noise is used in a mobile military lab to mask what is going on inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White noise' looks like one phrase, but 'white' belongs to the definition and only 'noise' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Albinoism, a variant of albinism, is the congenital lack of pigment that leaves skin and hair pale.

clue.text: Might this be read smoothly after taking a seat?

definitions.text: Might this be read smoothly after taking a seat?

indicators.note: taking a away from the word means its letter A is removed
might asks whether the words could become the answer once the letters are allowed to move around

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, losing its A

explanation.surface: A familiar tale flows easily when read aloud once you have sat down comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters are those of READ SMOOTHLY plus SET (seat with its A taken). The whole clue also hints at a familiar tale read easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A story told so often that it reads effortlessly is the proverbial tired, much-repeated tale.

clue.text: Revolving section becomes looser, say, and swings

indicators.note: revolving turns something round, so the word for a portion is written backwards
say tells us to speak the phrase and take a word pronounced the same

blocks.note: a part is a section
eases means slackens or loosens

explanation.surface: A rotating part works itself loose and starts swinging about.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from ropes for acrobats, so the plural names a set of circus swings.

clue.text: Give too much money for dodgy Devon fur

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shady, so the letters are not to be trusted in their given order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone overpays for a suspect pelt from Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To overfund something is to supply more cash than it needs, which is giving excessive financial support.

clue.text: Get a Times and an Independent in the centre

indicators.note: in the centre places the letter for the newspaper in the middle of the two-letter word

blocks.note: taken as written
T stands for time; read as a plural it is doubled
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for Independent

explanation.surface: Pick up a copy of The Times and The Independent, two British newspapers, at the shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A + TT + A(I)N; the surface treats Times and Independent as newspapers, but each gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain is to achieve or reach a goal, matching 'get' in the sense of obtain.

clue.text: Is this like The Goodies convention?

blocks.note: goodies are treats, read here as the singular word
the suffix -y makes an adjective meaning like, as in silky

explanation.surface: A question about whether this resembles The Goodies, a 1970s British TV comedy trio.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, a word meaning 'treat-like' would be TREAT + Y; the capitals on The Goodies are camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, and a convention is another term for such an international agreement.

clue.text: Most violent, having a hand in fight over queen and church

indicators.note: over means covering, so the clenched hand closes around what follows

blocks.note: a fist is a hand clenched for fighting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The most brutal combatant joins in a fight about the monarch and the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means aggressive and savage, so its superlative describes the most ferocious or violent.

clue.text: Before unruly teenager sat up, got a smack

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rebellious 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: Before the rowdy teen sat up straight, they were given a slap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the teenager after the reversed sitting word. 'Smack' looks like a blow but means a flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a taste or flavour, so getting a smack of something is experiencing its flavour, as when one tasted it.

clue.text: Couples leave trunk road finally for Cornish city

indicators.note: couples are pairs, so two letters at a time go from each word
finally shows the pairs removed are the ones at the end of each word

blocks.note: taken as written, losing its last two letters
taken as written, losing its last two letters

explanation.surface: Couples drive off the main highway at last, heading to a city in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: A trunk road is a British main road; TRU(NK) + RO(AD).
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the only city in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip, and its cathedral seat.

clue.text: I retired in Provence, lacking aspiration to play the bully and bouncer

indicators.note: retired means withdrew or went back, so the French pronoun is written backwards
aspiration is the breathy H sound, so lacking it drops the H

blocks.note: je is French for I
surface padding: Provence is in France, telling us to use the French word
to hector is to bully or browbeat

explanation.surface: A retired person in the south of France gives up their old habit of bullying people.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer throws unwanted people out of a club, and an ejector is anyone who throws people out.

clue.text: Sort of switch retaining energy, seconds and originals

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the switch type keeps the energy symbol within it

blocks.note: an on-off switch is a common sort
E is the symbol for energy in physics
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A type of switch that saves energy is listed alongside seconds and originals, as in a shop's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: ON(E)OFF + S: 'seconds and originals' reads like a list of goods, but seconds gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a unique item made only once, so such things are originals with no copies.

clue.text: Put in parking to increase business

blocks.note: to enter data is to put it in
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Installing a car park to boost trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a company or commercial undertaking, so it is a synonym for a business.

clue.text: She's constrained in manner

indicators.note: constrained in means held tightly within, so the name lies inside the following word

blocks.note: the inner letters of this word

explanation.surface: A woman is restricted in how she behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a female first name, so any woman called that could be referred to by the pronoun she.
